**Finding: Compliant** — no MFN obligation burdening us.

- **What I checked:** the fee-tier schedule (p0058–p0063), time-of-payment and audit terms (p0064–p0073), Supplemental Payments (p0074–p0083), rebate shares (p0075–p0076), support/enhancement pricing (p0086–p0095), and full-text searches for "favorable/favourable", "most favored", "best", "discount", "other licensees", "any other customer", "third party", "offer", "exclusiv".
- **Result:** the commercial terms are fixed-consideration and revenue-share mechanics (per-US$1m tiered fees; flat 33% share of defined third-party earnings). Nothing benchmarks our pricing or terms to what we give third parties, and nothing requires us to match a third-party offer made to the Licensor. The one "other licensees" reference (p0094, Revisions made available when generally released to other licensees) runs **in our favour**, so per the rule it is left untouched.
- **Noted but out of scope:** Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139–p0141) and the Change of Control consent/auto-termination (p0134) are genuine burdens on us at exit, but they are assignment/change-of-control controls rather than best-terms parity. I flagged them in the rationale for the relevant playbook rules instead of redlining them here.

No redline proposed, consistent with the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer).
